clue.text: A writer picking up The Master or Tarzan?

indicators.note: the writer's tool picks up, i.e. takes in, the next piece, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Is a novelist who takes up The Master (Toibin's Henry James novel) the same as a jungle hero?
explanation.walkthrough: The Master looks like Colm Toibin's novel about Henry James, but it is only the degree abbreviation, and 'picking up' means the pen takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan is the jungle man raised by great apes in Burroughs's stories.

clue.text: A music producer raised capital for Jaroslav Hasek?

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: a harp produces music

explanation.surface: A record producer raised money for a Czech writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hasek, author of The Good Soldier Svejk, was Czech; Praha is the Czech name for Prague.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the Czech capital, called Praha in Hasek's own language.

clue.text: Perm and a rinse grabs people like the Dubreuilhs

indicators.note: these words grab, i.e. hold within them, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A hairdo and a rinse catch the eye of a French couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dubreuilhs are a family in Simone de Beauvoir's novel The Mandarins.
explanation.definitionFit: De Beauvoir's novel names its Parisian intellectuals, the Dubreuilhs among them, after Chinese officials.

clue.text: Anna Wulf's blacklisted lover has gas about vacuous lovers

indicators.note: the gas goes about, i.e. around, the next piece

parts.note: neon is a gas

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: A heroine's banned lover has wind about empty-headed romantics.
explanation.walkthrough: In Doris Lessing's The Golden Notebook, Anna Wulf has an affair with Nelson, a blacklisted American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessing gives Anna Wulf an American lover of that name driven out by McCarthyism.

clue.text: Feel free to start angling like Robinson Crusoe?

definitions.meaning: an invitation to an angler to go ahead and throw the line out
Crusoe was marooned after a shipwreck, a lone survivor on an island

explanation.surface: An angler is told to get fishing, as a shipwrecked islander might.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked sailor left alone on an island, as Crusoe was, is the classic marooned figure.

clue.text: Sex columnist enhances dull cab trips

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A columnist on sex brightens boring taxi rides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' looks like the journeys but rearranges ENHANCES DULL CAB. Bushnell wrote the column that became Sex and the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Candace Bushnell wrote the New York Observer column Sex and the City.

clue.text: "Like the -, the peregrine lives in a pouring-away world of no attachment, a world of wakes and tilting, of sinking planes of land and water" (The Peregrine, JA Baker) ()

definitions.text: "Like the -, the peregrine lives in a pouring-away world of no attachment, a world of wakes and tilting, of sinking planes of land and water" (The Peregrine, JA Baker) ()

parts.words: "Like the -, the peregrine lives in a pouring-away world of no attachment, a world of wakes and tilting, of sinking planes of land and water" (The Peregrine, JA Baker) ()
parts.note: a quotation from J. A. Baker's The Peregrine with a gap for a word meaning a sailor, at home among wakes and tilting decks

explanation.surface: A passage from Baker's The Peregrine compares the falcon to someone at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner lives among wakes and tilting horizons, which is Baker's comparison for the falcon.

clue.text: Tea Party member is card, drinking large one

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the card holds the next pieces

parts.note: an ace is a playing card
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A political activist is quite a character, downing a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea Party suggests US politics, but it is the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's heroine attends the Mad Tea-Party with the Hatter and March Hare.

clue.text: Aunt wobbles around with broth for John Bull's biographer

indicators.note: wobbling around means unsteadily shifting, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt totters about with soup for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: John Arbuthnot created John Bull in The History of John Bull (1712).
explanation.definitionFit: Arbuthnot's satirical pamphlets invented and told the life of John Bull, emblem of England.

clue.text: A Livonian novel about northern WWII documentarian

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the next piece, enclosing it
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters before it take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book from the Baltic region is about a northern chronicler of the Second World War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges A LIVONIAN into VAINOLINA, and 'about' puts N inside it. Vaino Linna, the Finnish novelist, wrote The Unknown Soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Linna's novel The Unknown Soldier chronicles Finland's Continuation War against the Soviet Union in 1941-44.

clue.text: Old boy US soldier sent west to find Africans

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftwards, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
GI is the usual name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A former pupil who joined the American army is posted west to meet Africans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Igbo are a people of south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: A bag brought back by star in Playboy

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so this pair of pieces is read the other way

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: In a men's magazine, a handbag is returned by a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova, the Venetian seducer, is the archetypal womaniser.

clue.text: Fury found in contrary books written by smart chap

indicators.note: the books are written after the chap, so they follow him

parts.note: a smart alec is a know-all

indicators.note: contrary means the wrong way round, so the books are read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Anger is detected in perverse volumes by a clever fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Furies, the Greek avenging goddesses.

clue.text: Having dumped knight, went to bed with halos one British satirist

annotationWithheld.clue: Having dumped knight, went to bed with halos one British satirist

clue.text: Pay chap or put in a new order for religious books

indicators.note: putting things in a new order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Wages for a man, or rearranging the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical writings outside the Hebrew canon.

clue.text: Around noon, help with tea cooking princely snake food?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece, enclosing it
cooking means being prepared or concocted, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: At midday, help with making tea fit for a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the two words into ELEPHAT, and 'Around' wraps it round the noon letter. In Saint-Exupery's The Little Prince a boa constrictor swallows a huge beast whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Prince opens with a drawing of a boa that has swallowed a large grey beast whole.

clue.text: Marx Brother joke with Boomer ultimately and Queeqeg?

parts.note: Harpo was the silent Marx Brother
a one is a joke, as in 'that's a good one'

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A comedian's gag with a baby boomer and a whaling character.
explanation.walkthrough: Queequeg (spelt Queeqeg here) is the harpoonist of the Pequod in Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Melville's Queequeg throws the spear at whales from the Pequod's boats.

clue.text: Concerning problem ruining originally successful publisher?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an issue is a problem

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: About a difficulty that wrecked a once-prosperous publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: A firm that brings out books again tends to choose titles that were successful the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm bringing out new editions of past hits issues books a second time.

clue.text: Pinching son, provoke a posh thinker

indicators.note: pinching means nabbing, so the first word holds the next one inside it

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or provoke
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Stealing a boy, one might stir up an upper-class philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the Genevan philosopher of The Social Contract.

clue.text: Father of an onanist in violent exasperation, I hear

indicators.note: what one hears is a sound-alike, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: wrath is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Someone's father is said to be in a fury over his son's self-abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Roth created Alexander Portnoy, whose compulsive masturbation drives Portnoy's Complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is the literary parent of his character, here the self-pleasuring Portnoy.

clue.text: Nurse with Pynchon novel and topless playthings for diplomats

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
V. is Thomas Pynchon's first novel

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, which in a down entry is the first letter

parts.note: toys are playthings

explanation.surface: A nurse with a Pynchon book and bare-chested toys for embassy staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Envoys are diplomatic messengers sent abroad.

clue.text: Teacher primarily getting buns for Tom, Bert and William?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: rolls are bread buns

explanation.surface: A teacher brings bread for three pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom, Bert and William are the three trolls turned to stone in Tolkien's The Hobbit.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Hobbit three cave giants of that name try to cook the dwarves.

clue.text: Chap who wrote Hamlet in linearly ordered structure, I'm told

indicators.note: what one is told is heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a list is items in a single sequence

explanation.surface: The author of Hamlet set out in a tidy sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet suggests Shakespeare, but Franz Liszt wrote a symphonic poem called Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Liszt composed the symphonic poem Hamlet in 1858.

clue.text: "Children almost always things tighter than their parents think they will " (EB White)

definitions.text: "Children almost always things tighter than their parents think they will " (EB White)

parts.words: "Children almost always things tighter than their parents think they will " (EB White)
parts.note: a quotation from E. B. White with a missing two-word verb phrase meaning cling or keep hold of

explanation.surface: A quotation from E. B. White about how children keep hold of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing phrase means keep a grip on, completing White's observation about children.

clue.text: Eva was one right to punch illicit ticket seller

indicators.note: punching means going into, so this letter goes into the next piece

parts.note: a tout sells tickets unofficially

explanation.surface: A woman was right to hit a ticket scalper.
explanation.walkthrough: Eva Trout is the heroine and title of Elizabeth Bowen's last novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowen's novel is named for its heroine, so she is a fish by surname.

clue.text: What one can find in a bookshop: Ustinov work

indicators.note: what can be found inside these words is a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A Peter Ustinov book is the kind of thing one finds in a bookshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a composition or artistic production.

clue.text: I speculated about Jakob in June show with no cast

indicators.note: cast as in thrown about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre production staged in June with nobody in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors, but it rearranges JUNE SHOW and NO. Uwe Johnson wrote Speculations about Jakob (1959).
explanation.definitionFit: The German novelist wrote Mutmassungen uber Jakob, so he is the one who speculated.

clue.text: A short tale set in China depicting rural life

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the next

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate, so pal

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A brief story is located in China, showing country living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STORY to STOR. China is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral art and poetry idealise shepherds and the countryside.

clue.text: Magical being in place hosting piano recital at front

indicators.note: the place hosts, i.e. holds, the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a site is a place
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: at front means the leading letter only

explanation.surface: A fairy is found in a venue that puts on piano recitals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy.
